applyTo: "docs/changes/**/agent-tasks/*.md"

# CIS agent execution authority

- `docs/references/agent-provider-profile.md` defines enabled providers, transports, isolation, timeout, and maximum permissions; credentials remain provider-native.
- Direct execution requires an approved plan, accepted impacts, and a ready or in-progress task. The global design barrier blocks downstream work, not coordination, wireframe, or visual-design preparation needed to establish it.
- Select provider, mode, permission, target, transport, actor, and rationale explicitly. Availability is not authorization.
- Workspace-write execution uses an isolated Git worktree, seeded from the exact tracked and non-ignored untracked source baseline when dirty, unless the reviewed profile explicitly permits direct dirty-working-tree execution.
- `--approve-requests` covers explicitly authorized supported Codex requests within the declared ceiling. Claude uses optional per-attempt `--allow-command` rules for implementation with workspace-write; unsupported providers and read-only runs reject them. Native rules are additive and do not impose full shell, filesystem or network confinement. Inspect invoked scripts and native permissions. A permission-required result is failure, not a pending approval prompt.
- Runs, attempts, events, permissions, process identity, artifact hashes, and results are durable derived evidence under `.cis/local/agents/runs/`.
- Cancellation and resumption append provenance. They never discard the first attempt or rewrite canonical Markdown. Resupply explicit command rules on each resumed attempt; native session context restarts when either attempt uses them.
- Governed story implementation, review and corrections share the existing canonical change/task allocation across retries and owned repositories. Inspect `story work-status`; establish a missing association through `story bind-work --input` against existing approved work, without inventing allocation. Generic `agent resume` redirects story stages to governed story continuation.
- An exact registered owned participant's controls or retained story correction history permit finite allocation at the authority against existing approved canonical work. Establishing that allocation adopts work accounting for every supported direct-task and story route there, including siblings without correction history: each needs its canonical owner and applicable finite allocation. It does not adopt engineering quality policy or grant plan, design or completion approval. Reconcile displayed historical effort before reuse or a specific bounded correction grant.
- An explicit new task-time decision by the original allocation authority uses `cis agent work amend-time <change-id> <owner-task-id> --input <amendment.json> --actor <original-authority> --reason <rationale>`. Supply absolute `seconds`, the actual new `decisionReference` and fresh `expectedRevision`; delegated controller access alone is insufficient. The containing-change ceiling and all consumption, reservations, reserves, attempts, storage, flags, bindings and independent holds remain effective. Inspect the returned amendment reference and both remaining limits before execution; ordinary `allocate` still preserves fixed caps.
- `controller-assessment-required` means the authorized orchestrating agent must inspect retained implementation, failed/valid review evidence, measured cost, reservations, remaining capacity and current revision, then use `cis agent work progress <change-id> <task-id> --input <assessment.json> --actor <controller>` at the existing canonical owner. Record Outcome, nonempty Evidence, Approach, Decision and the next bounded action; CIS supplies measured Cost. Keep `closeAttempt: false` unless actually closing the logical attempt, then resume the governed story. No routine human acknowledgment, extra reviewer or task `Blocked` transition is required. Automatic `story-execution-summary` and legacy `story-controller-progress` records never qualify; candidate reuse gives no reflection credit. Explicit controller progress retains its owner-wide meaning; incidental story summaries cannot satisfy direct-task reflection. Status reads are non-mutating, and independent holds and counters remain binding.
- Two automatic story correction rounds remain durable. Correct required findings only; optional advice creates no mandatory changes or answers. New task reviews must state disposition and supporting basis independently of severity. Resolve inconsistent verdicts through the same bounded review context. Relevant controller disposition can permit one bounded next step, preserving prior rounds, costs and independent holds.
- Granted correction and review requests carry the authorized hypothesis, action and disposition provenance. Recovery/extensions retain prior direction, round identity, compatible stages and spent work; missing legacy direction requires exact-disposition recovery or the reported bounded `simplify` reconciliation. Nested stages created by the governed story or correction controller may use remaining whole seconds below 30, rounded down within admitted parent/correction deadlines; preparation remains charged. Direct `cis agent run` requests, including `--parent-execution`, and new root requests retain the 30-second minimum; direct requests must fit the parent's remainder without automatic shortening. Early retry failure retains legacy findings and still-current response provenance; material changes invalidate answers, and a valid newer empty review supersedes obsolete findings. Responses never waive required defects or approve completion.
- Apply the canonical code-quality standard's proportionate implementation policy. Material product responsibility or verification-machinery expansion receives an explicit necessity conclusion in the existing review; ordinary helpers need only concise not-applicable reasoning, not another ceremony. Unsupported responsibilities can be corrected by removal or a narrower promise.
- A provider result is untrusted evidence. Import it explicitly and preserve CIS as the only authority for plan approval, design approval, task transitions, verification, and final acceptance.
- Native mutation/incremental execution uses the same canonical work owner and inclusive allowance. Inherit a verified live CIS parent or supply `--change`, `--task`, `--actor` and applicable `--authority`; missing authority or finite numeric storage policy holds before preparation. Profiles never allocate capacity. Before broadening native mutation, inspect current baseline/kill/survivor/infrastructure/restored-health/claimed-child evidence and cost, then record substantive controller progress with the displayed `native-pilot:<basis>` reference. Keep native validity, threshold and qualification distinct; compatible material evidence survives bookkeeping changes. Count total declared owned outputs, agent/archive/retrieval data and scratch; review the existing cleanup plan and delegation, preserving protected/current/recovery/accounting and user material. `--recovery-of` restores only the original recipe/postflight within its existing reserve/attempt. Native cancellation retains uncertain reservations. Supported native/artifact monitoring is bounded and sampled; raw external sessions and arbitrary provider writes are outside that enforcement.
- Ordinary unit retry uses the same retained owner under the native invocation lock after prior accounting settles; stale activity alone does not require mutation restoration. For interrupted disposable unit work, first establish process cleanup or retirement of its disposable execution environment and resources, then record `abandon-native-unit` with the exact root/current revision/controller/reason and factual evidence. It preserves unknown historical facts, valid completed results, legitimate cost and used attempts; known live conflicts still block. Historical machine custody and boot attestation are not prerequisites for this controlled disposal. Inspect remaining capacity before retry; no new allowance is granted. Read-only storage inspection follows retained ownership even when the task is Blocked or retired.
- On Linux, use the existing native cancellation and reconciliation path with the actual worker session recorded before its launch gate opens. Stop its live process groups and verified driver/controller identities; reconcile only after the recorded owners and session have stopped. Driver absence alone is insufficient. This covers the trusted runner, not deliberately detached code. Missing historical session bindings stay unknown; controlled unit retirement remains available under its existing conditions.
- Check each original operation growth grant separately from the shared owned ceiling. Exact verified original restoration may pass a repeated-blocker exploration hold within its existing recipe/reserve/attempt; preserve that hold and history for subsequent exploration. Other capacity, uncertainty and permission holds remain binding.
